clue.text: A moral purge modified indoor pastime

indicators.note: something modified has been altered, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, all eleven letters

explanation.surface: A moral purge has been watered down into something you could play indoors on a rainy evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades or charades-like games played in the drawing room are the classic example of a pastime kept indoors.

clue.text: A line initially sprinted over too

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for line

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of sprinted
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An athlete who sprinted over a line as well, as if crossing the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs meaning in addition or as well, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Lout pursuing goal — ultimately do nothing

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the lout word is placed after the other piece
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of goal
an oaf is a clumsy lout

explanation.surface: A yob chasing after a football goal, yet in the end he does nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to idle about lazily, spending time without any useful activity.

clue.text: A French inlet not in good condition

parts.note: un is French for a
a sound is a narrow sea inlet or channel

explanation.surface: A French bay or estuary that is in poor shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound describes something damaged, decayed or unreliable, such as a structure or argument in poor repair.

clue.text: Kind, but not posh, Roman clan

indicators.note: but not asks for one element to be taken away from the word given

parts.note: a genus is a kind or class
U means upper-class, hence posh

explanation.surface: A sort of Roman family that is not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: U for posh comes from the 1950s distinction between U (upper-class) and non-U usage in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a gens was a group of families sharing a common name and claimed ancestor.

clue.text: Dull surface fine coating cold pickaxe

parts.note: a matt finish is dull, not glossy

indicators.note: a coating covers something all round, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: OK means fine or acceptable
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A paint job: a dull finish with a fine coat on a cold pickaxe.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattock is a digging tool with a broad blade, very like a pickaxe, used for breaking ground.

clue.text: When ill, swig rum to produce positive thoughts

indicators.note: rum is an old word for odd or strange, so the letters are oddly reordered

parts.note: the fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: Advice to knock back some rum when sick to cheer yourself up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink being swigged, but it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-wishing is the expression of kindly hopes for someone's welfare, a benevolent frame of mind.

clue.text: Accommodation manager curiously ogled goalie

indicators.note: curiously means in a strange way, so the word that follows is rearranged

parts.note: fodder for the rearrangement
a goalkeeper is a keeper

explanation.surface: A hotel manager oddly eyed up the football team's goalkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge-keeper looks after the gatehouse or lodge at the entrance to an estate, managing that dwelling.

clue.text: Forbid chaotic vote

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: fodder

explanation.surface: Blocking a ballot that has descended into disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to prohibit or reject a proposal by exercising authority.

clue.text: Eliminate pair of nincompoops in a hollow tussle

parts.note: two asses, an ass being a fool
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inside, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of tussle

explanation.surface: Getting rid of two idiots in a pointless scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliminate is used as a euphemism for killing, and to assassinate is to murder a prominent figure.

clue.text: Draw attention to showy plant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mark something for notice
second meaning: an iris, a plant with showy flowers

explanation.walkthrough: The yellow flag is a wild iris common in British wetlands.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means mark or highlight for attention; as a noun it names an iris with striking blooms.

clue.text: I travel by spectacle containing constant play of rainbow colours

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the spectacle word wraps round the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
to ride is to travel by horse or vehicle
a scene is a spectacle or view
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Someone travelling by a spectacular sight that keeps flashing rainbow hues.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescence is the shimmering display of changing spectral colours seen on soap bubbles or oil films.

clue.text: Obstinate son kissed amorously after squabble

indicators.note: after tells us the kissing word follows the squabble word in order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a tiff is a petty quarrel
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: A lad making up with his girlfriend after a row, kissing passionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff-necked describes someone haughtily stubborn, refusing to bend, as an unyielding neck will not.

clue.text: Consider again queen around weak king

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the queen abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
a thin argument is a weak one
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A queen thinking again about a feeble monarch beside her.
explanation.definitionFit: To rethink is to reconsider a plan or opinion, weighing it a second time.

clue.text: Foreign currency showing up in manor kitty

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top
showing means visible inside the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Foreign money appearing in the household kitty at the big house.
explanation.definitionFit: The krona is the currency unit of Sweden and Iceland, so foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Reserve early, essentially, in primarily key site of winter sport

parts.note: ice means coldness of manner, reserve

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the central letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the central letter of early
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the initial letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the first letter of key

explanation.surface: Booking ahead at an important venue for winter sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' reads as book, but here it is the noun meaning aloofness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice rink is a frozen surface for skating, curling or ice hockey, all winter sports.

clue.text: Popular umpire turns up to conclude from evidence

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the umpire word is flipped to read upwards

parts.note: a ref is a referee, an umpire

explanation.surface: A well-liked match official arrives to draw conclusions from what he sees.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or reason out a conclusion from facts available.

clue.text: Absorbed order by Democrat

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
to rank is to put in order

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in an instruction issued by a US Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbed' looks like engrossed, but it means swallowed or soaked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink is to take in liquid, so what was drunk has been soaked up or swallowed.

clue.text: Remove some appointed officers

indicators.note: some means part of the words that follow, so a stretch of them is used

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Taking away a few officials who were appointed.
explanation.definitionFit: To doff is to take off a garment, especially a hat in greeting.

clue.text: Mum loves occasionally leaving Oxford?

parts.note: mum as in keep mum: silent, so a call for quiet

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of loves

explanation.surface: A mother who adores the occasional trip away from Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, but it is the word for silent, as in keep mum. The question mark flags Oxford as an example rather than the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe, so the city name stands for one instance of footwear.

clue.text: Article on hair cosmetic, bringer of good news

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
styling gel for hair

explanation.surface: A magazine piece on hair products that brings welcome tidings.
explanation.definitionFit: In scripture angels are messengers, as when Gabriel announced glad tidings; the Greek root means messenger.

clue.text: Fan, say, of unemotional and relaxed backing tune

indicators.note: in a down clue backing means supporting from below, so that piece goes underneath

parts.note: an air is a melody
cool means both calm and unemotional

explanation.surface: An admirer of a chilled, laid-back melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' reads as an enthusiast, but here it is the verb: fanning is one way to cool with moving air.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanning is an example of cooling by a current of air, hence the 'say' marking an instance.

clue.text: Shy essayist's plant

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to lob
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A timid writer's garden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid, but it is the verb to throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden bedding flower, often blue, so a particular example of a plant.

clue.text: A grain's converted for an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Cereal turned into booze, as a distiller would.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Papal church tale of chivalry

parts.note: Roman as in Roman Catholic, of the Pope
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A legend about knights told by the Pope's church.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval romance is a narrative of knightly adventure and courtly love.

clue.text: Pinkish-yellow fruit not initially for everyone

indicators.note: not initially means without its opening letter

parts.note: a peach is a pinkish-yellow fruit

explanation.surface: Peaches without the first one shared out to all.
explanation.definitionFit: Priced at so much apiece means the cost per person or item, an adverbial sense covering everyone.

clue.text: Jog back to right

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
RT is an abbreviation of right

explanation.surface: A runner jogging back over to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot is to run at a gentle, steady pace, like a jogger or a horse.

clue.text: Desire topless charmer

indicators.note: topless means with the top removed; in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: a witch casts charms, so is a charmer

explanation.surface: Lust for a seductive woman who has no top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charmer' suggests a seductive person, but here it is a spell-caster.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or urge, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: Urban area to west and north

parts.note: taken as written
compass abbreviation
compass abbreviation
joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A built-up area lying to the west and north.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a settlement larger than a village, a built-up place where people live and work.

clue.text: Blimey! Start of real euphoria in interdependence

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of the next word only

parts.note: first letter of real
elation is great joy

explanation.surface: An exclamation of astonishment at the onset of real ecstasy in a close relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: Blimey and cor are both informal British exclamations of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A correlation is a mutual relationship where two things vary together, a kind of interdependence.

clue.text: Propeller failing to start for ship's company

indicators.note: failing to start means missing its opening letter

parts.note: a ship's screw is its propeller

explanation.surface: A propeller that will not turn, a problem for those aboard the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing to start' paints an engine fault but signals losing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's crew is the body of sailors who work aboard her, its company of hands.

clue.text: No alchemist manipulated this vending apparatus

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and changed about, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: fodder, eleven letters

explanation.surface: No alchemist could turn this coin machine into gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot machine takes coins through a slot to dispense goods or play a game, a coin-operated vending device.
